verdict: UDR's rent revenue dipped 1% to $428M as sold properties left the portfolio, but a $190M gain on property sales lifted net income to $231M, while FFO as Adjusted held at $0.65 a share.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: total revenue $428M vs $432M a year ago — property sales offset same-store revenue growth of 1.8%

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: net income per diluted share, vs $0.12 a year ago — lifted by the $190M gain on property sales

kpis.label: FFOA per share
kpis.note: Funds from Operations as Adjusted (non-GAAP), flat vs a year ago; FFO was $0.62

kpis.label: Same-store NOI growth
kpis.note: net operating income at long-held properties rose 1.6% YoY, with occupancy of 96.5%

segments.name: Rental income
segments.note: Rent from residents at UDR's apartment communities — down 1% YoY because communities that were sold stopped contributing, even though same-store rent grew.

segments.name: Joint venture & other fees
segments.note: Fees for managing properties owned with partners, and other fee income — $3.5M on the statement, shown as $3M after rounding so the segments tie to the $428M total.

opex.name: Real estate depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of the apartment buildings over their accounting lives — the big non-cash cost that makes REIT GAAP profit look small next to FFO. The statement line is $162M ($161,569K); shown as $161M so the rounded flow ties.

opex.name: Property management
opex.note: Running the property-management platform that operates the communities.

opex.name: Other operating expenses
opex.note: Other day-to-day operating costs not listed separately.

opex.name: Casualty-related charges
opex.note: Storm and casualty costs at properties, net of recoveries.

otherDetail: A $190M gain on sale of real estate owned, plus $8M of interest and other income and $2M of income from unconsolidated entities, less $49M of interest expense — a net $151M. On UDR's statement the $190M gain sits above operating income; here it is shown below the operating line because it is a one-off, so operating income here is the $80M earned from running properties.
follow100Note: Tax was $489K — about 11 cents per $100 of revenue — so it appears here at its true size even though it rounds to $0M in the flow above; that is why the waterfall lands $0.11 short of the $53.97 kept as profit. Depreciation takes $38.32 of every $100 (the $161M real-estate line plus $3M other) — which is why REIT investors watch FFO, which adds most depreciation back: FFO as Adjusted was $0.65 per share versus $0.67 of GAAP EPS, the closeness here only because the $190M sales gain flatters GAAP.

takeaways.title: Property deals drove GAAP profit
takeaways.text: UDR booked a $190M gain on sale of real estate owned in a quarter of heavy deal-making: it sold two communities for $183M and closed a $2.0B joint venture with Apollo, contributing 19 communities and receiving $1.34B of equity capital. That gain is why net income jumped to $231M from $43M a year ago.

takeaways.title: The rent business grew steadily
takeaways.text: Same-store revenue rose 1.8% and same-store NOI rose 1.6%, with occupancy at 96.5% and bad debt improving. Total revenue still fell 1% because sold properties no longer contribute rent.

takeaways.title: FFOA flat, guidance raised
takeaways.text: FFO as Adjusted was $0.65 per diluted share, flat year over year, and FFO was $0.62. UDR raised its full-year net income guidance sharply — to $1.58–$1.60 a share — on the sales gains, and nudged FFOA guidance up to $2.54–$2.56.

oneTimers: Results include a $190M gain on sale of real estate owned — UDR sold two apartment communities (Seattle and Nashville, 412 homes, $183M of gross proceeds) and closed its Apollo joint venture in the quarter. Excluding such gains is exactly what FFO does, which is why FFO per share ($0.62) barely moved while GAAP EPS jumped to $0.67 from $0.12.
footerNote: UDR is a REIT: this flow ties to total GAAP net income of $231M before allocations — $15M went to redeemable noncontrolling interests and about $1M to preferred dividends, leaving $215M of net income attributable to UDR common stockholders ($0.67 per diluted share). FFO and FFOA are non-GAAP and appear in the KPIs and takeaways only. Cost of revenue is property operating costs excluding depreciation (property operating and maintenance of $81M plus real-estate taxes and insurance of $57M, from the 10-Q, rounded from thousands); tax was a $489K provision, which rounds to $0M.
